facts.heading: Daniel burned out October
facts.content: Daniel is a project manager burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to Leeds
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to neurology appointments in Leeds.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about fatigue
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty about being tired while his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill

facts.heading: Daniel hides fatigue from sister
facts.content: Daniel tells his sister Hannah he is fine despite being tired.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine

facts.heading: Daniel sleeps four hours nightly
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours

facts.heading: Daniel wakes at three am
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning

facts.heading: Daniel dreads the nights
facts.content: Daniel dreads the nights when he is awake.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest

facts.heading: Daniel sits in car park
facts.content: Daniel sometimes sits in the hospital car park before entering.
facts.evidence: I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in

facts.heading: Daniel's father has Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn

facts.heading: Daniel's sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto

facts.heading: Daniel does three people's jobs
facts.content: Daniel ended up doing three people's jobs after a client loss.
facts.evidence: so I ended up doing three people's jobs

facts.heading: Daniel works until ten at night
facts.content: Daniel is still answering messages at ten at night.
facts.evidence: I'm still answering messages at ten at night

facts.heading: Daniel thinks about work constantly
facts.content: Daniel thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work

facts.heading: Daniel's father is seventy-three
facts.content: Daniel's father is seventy-three years old.
facts.evidence: He's seventy-three

facts.heading: Daniel's father's hands shake
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake and he is slower.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower

facts.heading: Daniel's father gets frustrated
facts.content: Daniel's father gets frustrated with his condition.
facts.evidence: and he gets frustrated

facts.heading: Daniel's father was the strong one
facts.content: Daniel's father has always been the strong one in the family.
facts.evidence: he's always been the strong one

facts.heading: Daniel feels neglected by sister
facts.content: Daniel feels his sister Hannah is neglecting him by not being there.
facts.evidence: It's just that I'm the one who's here

facts.heading: Daniel cannot face hospital visits
facts.content: Daniel cannot face entering the hospital for his father's appointments.
facts.evidence: because I can't face it

facts.heading: GP diagnosed stress and exhaustion
facts.content: Daniel's GP found normal blood tests and attributed his condition to stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Daniel refused therapy initially
facts.content: Daniel told his GP he did not have time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: I said I hadn't got time

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire booked Daniel's session
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire booked his therapy session because she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire.

facts.heading: Claire makes Daniel tea
facts.content: Claire makes tea for Daniel and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away for the weekend because he always says no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend, because I always say no.

facts.heading: Daniel fears missing emails when away
facts.content: Daniel worries that if he is away, he will receive two hundred emails.
facts.evidence: If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them.

facts.heading: Daniel worries about his father
facts.content: Daniel worries that his father might need something if he is away.
facts.evidence: And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Daniel stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running ten kilometres every Saturday morning about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago.

facts.heading: Daniel ran for six years before October
facts.content: Daniel ran ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years before October.
facts.evidence: I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Daniel feels he lost a part of himself
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself since he stopped running.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Daniel felt unreachable while running
facts.content: Daniel felt that running was the one time in the week nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Daniel works for Peterson
facts.content: Daniel works for a boss named Peterson who sends emails at eleven at night.
facts.evidence: Peterson. He's all right as a person, but he sends emails at eleven at night

facts.heading: Daniel answers Peterson's emails at night
facts.content: Daniel answers Peterson's emails every time, even if he is in bed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Claire hates Daniel answering emails at night
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire hates it when Daniel answers Peterson's emails at night.
facts.evidence: Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Daniel fears being let go due to restructuring
facts.content: Daniel is afraid they will let him go because of a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Daniel has a mortgage
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage and is worried about losing his job.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Daniel had heart symptoms during an outburst
facts.content: Daniel's heart was going and his hands were shaking when he snapped at a colleague.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Daniel thought he might have a heart attack
facts.content: Daniel thought for a second he was having a heart attack but it passed.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Daniel felt relief from talking
facts.content: Daniel felt relief and described it as putting down a heavy bag.
facts.evidence: A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Daniel drinks six cups of coffee daily
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: Coffee, probably. I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Daniel drinks wine to switch off
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine in the evenings to switch off.
facts.evidence: I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Daniel feels uneasy about drinking wine
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy about the wine because it stops working after an hour.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Daniel wants to stop the nights
facts.content: Daniel wants to stop the nights because he thinks he could cope if he could sleep.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Daniel has a stoic family background
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather and father worked in mines and never complained, telling people to just get on with it.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once. Dad's the same. You just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel believes he is weak for seeking help
facts.content: Daniel keeps thinking his grandfather would think he is weak for being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Daniel plans to try a phone switch-off
facts.content: Daniel plans to try switching off his phone at half past nine for twenty minutes.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Daniel plans to write a nightly note
facts.content: Daniel plans to write down when he wakes up if he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Daniel feels tired but lighter after talking
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after talking about his issues.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.
